expectations.text: Addresses Jules, signs Nia, accurately gives $36 refund submitted today with usual 3–5 business days and no guarantee.
expectations.evidence: “Hi Jules”; “refund for your duplicate $36 delivery fee today”; “usually appears in 3–5 business days”; signed “Nia / Support Lead.”

expectations.text: States replacement scheduled to dispatch Friday without promising Friday delivery; tracking follows dispatch and no resubmission is needed.
expectations.evidence: “scheduled to leave our warehouse Friday”; “That's the dispatch date”; “send your tracking information after dispatch”; “don't need to resubmit the request.”

expectations.text: Does not reproduce debugging/blame chronology, second-option shorthand or writing directions.
expectations.evidence: The email contains refund/dispatch information and an apology (“sorry for the duplicate charge”); no engineering chronology, blame, second option or editorial instructions.

expectations.text: Does not claim a permanent fix or deployed prevention change, invent tracking or authorize a coupon.
expectations.evidence: No permanent fix/deployed change/coupon is claimed; “don't yet have ... tracking number” matches the source’s explicit lack of tracking.

expectations.text: Does not turn unsupplied logistics information into an assertion that it is absent or unknown to the sender; preserves the difference between source omission and real-world status.
expectations.evidence: “we don't yet have a delivery date” asserts a real-world information gap absent from the thread, which supplies only that Friday is dispatch rather than a delivery promise.

critical_failures: Unsupported current logistics status: “we don't yet have a delivery date” is not supplied by the thread. Absence of a date in the source does not establish the sender lacks one.
review_method: Independent single blind agent review; not human feedback
